question: site-electrical-reticulation
unit: sum (whole external reticulation installation, 250 m route, GST exclusive, Auckland)

band.unit: sum (whole external reticulation installation, 250 m route, GST exclusive, Auckland)
band.basis: $83,000 - $128,000 (centre ~$106,000), GST exclusive, Auckland, QV CostBuilder rates plus labelled allowances, excluding preliminaries, margin, design and consent fees per the fixed exclusions. Component split so parts can be rejected individually: trenching/reinstatement 12.7-24.7k; conduit+draw cord+cable+terminations 57.6-78.4k; pits 8.0-16.0k; board+plinth+spurs+testing 4.9-9.1k. Allowances total 10.6-22.8k (~15% of centre), so the band rests mainly on the cited QV rows, not on allowances. Implied rate over the 250 m nominal route: low $332/m, centre $424/m, high $512/m. Confidence low: all QV rows are unreviewed, QV's buried-conduit rates are non-monotonic with diameter and appear high against current wholesaler pricing for 63 mm heavy-duty conduit, and the pit group has no published NZ price. This is a cost-plan band, not a certified price.

band.unit: sum (whole external reticulation installation, one site, 250m nominal route)
band.basis: Auckland, GST exclusive, no preliminaries, margin or design. Built by adding distinct components, each either a cited QV row (unreviewed, caveated), a fetched vendor figure, or a named allowance; no published total or aggregate row is added on top of its own parts, and no part already inside a cited rate (marker tape in the conduit row, end terminations in the sub-main item) is charged twice. Group subtotals: trenching/reinstatement $13,036-$27,096; conduit and cable $56,800-$84,970; pits $11,000-$18,000; board, plinth, spurs and compliance $5,650-$10,450. Implied rate over the 250m nominal route: about $345/lm (low), $450/lm (centre), $560/lm (high), so the amortisation is auditable. Allowances carry about 7-8% of the band (backfill/spoil, draw cord, testing/CoC) - under one third. Confidence is low, not because the main drivers are unsourced but because (i) QV electrical rows are unreviewed and internally inconsistent, (ii) the sub-main has no QV row and its band spans a vendor material build-up and a copper-uplifted QV aluminium proxy, and (iii) the polymer pits and Class B/C lids are proxied from precast cesspit and cast-iron cover rows. Reject any one of the four groups without disturbing the others.

Working cost-plan band for the fixed scope, GST exclusive, Auckland, at QV CostBuilder rates (rows cited, unreviewed) plus fetched vendor prices and labelled allowances. Sum of four rejectable parts: trenching and reinstatement $15,635-$28,195; conduit and cable $61,500-$72,500; pits $11,680-$19,820; board and spurs $9,337-$17,550. Implied rate over the 250 m nominal route: $393-$552 per lineal metre, centre approx. $472/lm. Allowances (draw cord, sub-main drawing-in/termination, pit surrounds, board uplift, plinth, board terminations, drop terminations, testing/CoC/as-built) are about 13% of the mid band, under the one-third threshold. Dominant exposure is the 750 m of buried conduit, priced from QV's 50 mm row with a stated size proxy for 63 mm; the 180 m 4-core sub-main is priced from a fetched NZ vendor page plus a labour allowance rather than QV's single-core copper rows. Mid band sits at the upper end of current market expectation for this scope because QV's installed electrical and drainage rates are generous; if tendering, expect the low end or below. Excludes GST, preliminaries, margin, design and consent fees, incoming supply/network/transformer/metering, poles, footings, luminaires, controls, CCTV/comms, rock, contaminated spoil, dewatering, traffic management, second sub-main/generator/EV and paving/kerbing/landscaping beyond the trench line.
